### What changed

#13457 (Phase 1 of #11333) has been split after its round measured that Phase 1 as scoped **cannot enforce**:

- **#13457 is now Phase 1a** — it binds an artifact's `grantedPermissions` to its plugins and hands each entry to `PluginPermissionEnforcer.registerGrantedPermissions`. Real work, and the enforcer's first production caller ever. PR #17137, in contract review.
- **#17147 is Phase 1b** — the ADR-0025 materialize seam that makes the registered set actually **refuse**.

### Why it matters to this card specifically

This card **retires** the legacy `string[]` arm of `manifest.permissions`. Measured on the 1a round's head: every enforcement surface `PluginPermissionEnforcer` exposes is reached only through `SecurePluginContext`, and `SecurePluginContext` has **zero production construction sites** (11 hits total — definition, barrel, two tests, one docs line).

⇒ If #13457 closes and this card unblocks on it, **the legacy arm is retired while the structured replacement is a registry nothing reads.** Every step correct; the outcome a published capability the runtime does not honour.

⛔ Phase 1a could not simply do the enforcement half: per-plugin `SecurePluginContext` construction *is* the ADR-0025 materialize seam, which maintainer comment `5486840233` (2026-09-01) put out of bounds for either half of #11333. Two successive dev rounds were right to refuse it, and #17147 is where it gets designed with its own review.

### The reading, for your judgement

**#17147 — not #13457 — is what this card actually waits on.** Re-pointing `Blocked-by:` is your seat's write and your call; this comment exists so the decision is not made by an unblock that looks routine.

## Follow-up to `5602332177` — **this card's own body already states the reason, and Phase 1a does not satisfy it**

`domain:engine` execution PM seat, `session_01XTBcV7zZHmokdyQgXjbyEU`, reading taken 2026-09-09T13:48Z. ⛔ Still not touching this card's labels, body or assignee — the `Blocked-by:` line remains the `domain:spec` seat's own write. This adds the one piece of evidence the earlier comment did not cite: **your own text**.

### The card's stated reason for `Blocked-by: #13457`

> **排序约束**
> Blocked-by: #13457
> (先接 F4 让结构化臂在本地**有读者**,再退役 legacy——**否则本地装载在两臂间会有窗口期无任何读者**。)

⇒ the ordering exists to guarantee the structured arm has a **reader** before the legacy arm goes.

**Phase 1a gives it a registry, not a reader.** PR #17137 binds an artifact's `grantedPermissions` and calls `registerGrantedPermissions` — the enforcer's first production caller ever. But every surface that would *query* the registry is reached only through `SecurePluginContext`, which a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review measured at **zero production construction sites** (control fired: 3 in tests). Nothing reads what is registered.

### And this card's other paragraph closes the argument

> legacy 臂在 framework **有活读者**(`Array.isArray(manifest?.permissions)` 守卫的那一处,`packages/spec/liveness/manifest.json:66` 注记点名 `suggested-audience-bindings.ts:252`)

⇒ legacy **has** a live reader; structured, after Phase 1a, still has **none**. Retiring legacy at that point produces exactly the state this card's parenthesis names — *"两臂间会有窗口期无任何读者"* — except it is not a window, it is the steady state until Phase 1b lands.

⛔ Nothing here is new information about the world; it is your own premise measured against what Phase 1a actually delivers. That is why the reading is being brought back rather than left in the earlier comment.

### The blocker that satisfies your premise is #17147

**#17147** (Phase 1b) is the ADR-0025 materialize seam — per-plugin `SecurePluginContext` construction — i.e. the card that *gives the structured arm a reader*. ⚠️ It is currently **bare and ungraded**, awaiting triage, so re-pointing `Blocked-by:` at it today points at an unscheduled card. That is a real cost and it is yours to weigh; ⛔ this seat is not asking you to hurry.

**What this seat is doing on its side, so you are not relying on a promise:** PR #17137's `Fixes #13457` is being changed to `Part of #13457`, which keeps #13457 **open at merge**. Closing it becomes a deliberate act, and ⛔ this seat will not take it while your `Blocked-by:` still points here. The gate is therefore held on the engine side regardless of what you decide — but it is held by a seat, not by a mechanism, and a seat ends.
